# opwan_dns (Resource)

opdns DNS: links the account's static addresses to an opdns profile, so lookups from them to `resolver` are filtered by it. The tunnel configuration doesn't change: point devices that use a static address at `resolver`. Needs an opdns account on the same op account. Destroying this resource turns opdns DNS off.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "opwan_dns" "this" {}

resource "opwan_dns" "this" {
  profile_id = one([for p in data.opwan_dns.this.profiles : p.id if p.name == "Family"])
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `profile_id` (String) An opdns profile id, from the `opwan_dns` data source's `profiles`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `dns`.
- `linked_ips` (List of String) The addresses opdns has linked to the profile now.
- `profile_name` (String) The profile's name.
- `resolver` (String) opdns's resolver address.
- `state` (String) `pending` (opdns not updated yet, opwan keeps trying), `linked` or `error`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The account has one DNS opt-in; its id is always "dns".
terraform import opwan_dns.this dns
```
